title: Director, AI Quality, Evaluation & Observability Engineering
text:
### **Why Patients Need You**

Pfizer's Commercial organization is putting GenAI and AI agents into work that shapes how medicines reach patients, from content creation and review to field and customer engagement. If we can't show that these systems are accurate, safe and behaving as intended, they don't belong in production. You will build the engineering capability that lets Pfizer prove it, before release and every day after.

### **What You Will Achieve**

You will own the evaluation and observability capability for AI solutions across the Commercial portfolio, and you will be accountable for the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards: the metrics, thresholds and technical criteria that inform production-readiness and ongoing monitoring decisions. You will build shared tooling, datasets and metrics that let product teams measure quality, safety and performance consistently, catch regressions before release, and detect drift and failures in production. You will set your team's priorities and decide where its engineering capacity goes across the portfolio. Success means teams evaluate through your platform by default, release decisions rest on evidence, and production AI issues are caught by monitoring before users or auditors find them.

### **How You Will Achieve It**

* Build and run a shared evaluation platform for GenAI and agentic solutions. It covers offline test suites, regression testing in CI/CD, LLM-as-judge and rubric-based scoring, and structured human review workflows.
* Set the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, including metrics for accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, safety, bias, robustness and task success and the minimum monitoring every production AI solution must have. Calibrate automated scoring against expert human judgment and publish the agreement rates.
* Partner with commercial technology leaders to create and govern golden datasets and test sets with domain experts (e.g., medical, legal and regulatory reviewers), including versioning, data lineage and handling of sensitive data.
* Implement production observability for AI systems, including tracing of prompts, retrievals, tool calls and agent steps, plus monitoring of quality, drift, latency, cost and guardrail activity, with alerting and incident response.
* Evaluate technical and model quality, with business outcomes and value measured separately.
* Set the evaluation thresholds and technical production-readiness criteria that feed release gates run by SDLC Standards & Governance, and give a clear pass, conditional or fail assessment against them, so go-live decisions rely on measured results rather than demos.
* Partner with Responsible AI, Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity and Compliance to turn policy requirements into measurable tests and auditable evidence, including support for AI-related audits and regulatory inquiries.
* Run adversarial and red-team testing (e.g., prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage) with Cybersecurity, and feed the findings back into evaluation suites.
* Evaluate models and vendors objectively when teams select or upgrade foundation models, AI platforms or third-party AI products in partnership with Strategic Partnerships and contracting, so vendor decisions stay joined up.
* Report quality and reliability trends across the AI portfolio to senior Digital and Commercial leadership.
* Set priorities for the AI quality and observability team and allocate its engineering capacity against portfolio needs, based on risk, release timing and business impact. Make the trade-offs visible and escalate when demand exceeds capacity.
* Lead and develop a team of AI quality and observability engineers that will evolve over time, and coach product and vendor teams, including third-party and offshore partners, to own their evaluations using shared tooling.

### **Decision Rights & Escalation**

* **Decides:** Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, metrics, thresholds and minimum monitoring requirements; the technical readiness assessment for each release; team priorities and capacity allocation; evaluation tooling and platform design within enterprise architecture standards.
* **Informs:** Release go/no-go decisions made through SDLC stage gates and product ownership; model, platform and vendor selection decisions led with Strategic Partnerships and contracting.
* **Escalates to the Commercial AI Portfolio Lead when:** a team wants to release a solution that does not meet agreed thresholds (risk acceptance); a production issue creates patient-safety, compliance or reputational exposure; demand for evaluation support exceeds team capacity across priority programs; or Responsible AI, Legal or Cybersecurity cannot agree on how a requirement becomes a test.

### **Qualifications**

**Must-Have**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience in software, ML or data engineering, including 3+ years building evaluation, testing or monitoring for ML or GenAI systems in production.
* Hands-on experience designing LLM evaluations, including rubric and LLM-as-judge methods, human evaluation design, and statistically sound comparison of model or prompt versions.
* Experience instrumenting production systems for observability (tracing, metrics, logging, alerting) and running incident response.
* Strong Python skills and experience integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
* Experience leading engineering teams and influencing product teams across a matrix without direct authority.
* Ability to explain evaluation results and their limits plainly to non-technical leaders.

**Nice-to-Have**

* Master's degree or PhD in a quantitative field.
* Experience with LLM evaluation and observability tooling (e.g., OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Arize, Weights & Biases, MLflow, Ragas, Promptfoo).
* Experience evaluating RAG systems and multi-step AI agents, including tool use and MCP-based integrations.
* Familiarity with AI risk and regulatory frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001).
* Experience with AI red-teaming or adversarial testing.
* Pharmaceutical or life sciences experience, ideally with Commercial, promotional review, medical or other regulated content.

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

**Other Job Details:**

* Last Date to Apply for Job: **December 7, 2026.**
* Ability to travel based on business needs
* This position is hybrid and requires working onsite 2 to 3 days per week

 
The annual base salary for this position ranges from $189,200.00 to $315,400.00.
